Unit interleavings additionally cover repeated retries, distinct identical legacy taps, failed identity persistence, concurrent drains and account switches.

A writer with no API key of their own asks for a resonance reading or a note's first letter in a production build (#3262). Since ADR 0009 phase (a) (#3067) BotMason credits pay only for a reading the writer's own vault answers, so the app reads GET /vault/connection before pricing a reading: when the server says nothing is attached, the disclosure leads with 'This needs your own API key', names no BotMason price, drops the 'don't show this again' box, and its Continue arm becomes Open Settings, which opens API-key settings -- even for a writer who dismissed the cost note, so no request is sent that the server can only refuse llm_key_required. A letter never goes to a vault, so its offer says the same without reading the vault or the wallet, and its ask becomes Open Settings. A reading a connected or managed vault may answer (or whose connection could not be read) keeps its shipped BotMason price line from GET /user/usage, and a saved key keeps 'Your own API key pays for this ...'. When that vault-answered reading meets an empty wallet, the refill dialog offers a key and, only when EXPO_PUBLIC_CREDIT_PACK_URL is set to an https page, 'or add more BotMason credits' with a link to the pack page and a note to buy with the same email address as the Adepthood account; unset, it says nothing about buying credits. Uncovered because the browser lane drives the Expo development server, where KEYLESS_GENERATION_REACHES_SERVER is true (its stub seam answers keyless requests, so the shipped price lines stay), and the lane arms BOTMASON_STUB_SEAM lane-wide, the same constraint journal.ai-refused-without-payer records. Pinned meanwhile by the Jest suites resonanceCost, JournalEntryScreenResonanceExplainer (the production-build describe), ResonanceRefillDialogPayer, creditPack and config.

An operator, not a user, decides whether a public privacy or product claim (C01-C24 in docs/legal/claim-ledger.json) may be published. The publish gate (backend/scripts/claim_certification.py, run by backend/tests/scripts/test_claim_publish_gate.py) refuses any ledger claim marked published without a current certificate in docs/qa/claim-certifications.json: an independent reviewer who implemented nothing and is not the loop, tested commits equal to the backend and frontend releases the serving receipts report, resolving non-xfail tests and covered journeys, passed dependency gates, a human signoff on the exact sentence digest, and an unexpired 90-day window. It renders no screen; the crossing below names the journal surface the strongest claims (C03, C07-C12, C20-C23) are about. Uncovered (#3076): no claim is certified, because certification needs an appointed independent human reviewer and live synthetic journeys on the serving build, both owner actions, so nothing can cross this seam yet.

The same browser signs up account A, declines all three device-local Journal offers through real Settings switches, reloads, logs out and signs up B. B starts with fresh choices. A returns with its declines intact, explicitly restores each offer, and reloads with the restore retained. Phone and desktop controls are then driven by keyboard at 200% actual text and frames are saved. This is device/account isolation and Settings persistence, not reinstall, cross-device synchronization or opaque Return episode identity. Legacy attribution and interrupted persistence are independently controlled in declineOwnership.test.ts and AuthContext.test.tsx.

A course invitation explains why it appeared: a theme across the writer's full corpus has crossed the generation threshold, and the reading is named by that stage's served Aspect rather than its relationship-to-free-will persona (#3104). The browser arranges a real pending course/readiness InvitationSignal whose target_id names stage 2, opens the Notification Center directly from a cold Journal route, and requires its one visit-free GET /stages/correspondence lookup to carry a deliberately long served Aspect while excluding a deliberately distinct served persona. The same real card stays fully readable with a clear one-tap Not now action at 390x844, at an effective 200% size, and at 1280x800; glyph bounds, viewport overflow, line/action separation, the 44px target, the unchanged spoken name and the real dismiss POST are asserted. Eligibility generation itself remains pinned by the backend domain suite; this journey begins from the persisted signal so it can isolate the frontend lookup and copy seam.

Real pending InvitationSignal rows are arranged in the isolated database, without pretending to prove eligibility or generation. The real browser loads GET /invitations, declines two different cards while one request is held, completes the other real POST, then injects a 503 only for the held request. Only the failed card returns in server order; the confirmed card stays absent. The browser retries the failed decline through the real POST and reloads; the real GET retains only the untouched card. Phone and desktop retry controls are keyboard driven at 200% text with frames saved. This covers the invitation persistence seam missing from the fresh-account journal-only proof (#3296).

Remaining #3073 acceptance: a Return decline and any retry must belong to both the account and the opaque server offer episode; an old answer cannot suppress a later eligible episode or be replayed to it after account replacement. The current device boolean cannot establish episode identity. This slice scopes other local Journal declines but deliberately leaves Return storage unchanged until GET /metta-return exposes an opaque episode and the dismiss POST validates the expected episode. Existing begin-a-return browser coverage proves the current decline route, not this missing contract.

#3275, Refs #3057/#3260 item4: real UI Intimate PATCH and DELETE cross the live backend to an isolated recording Creek contract process. A held remote withdrawal retains its fragment while PATCH503 commits Intimate and keeps editing; reload confirms only tier/prose, independently retained remote copy stays explicit. Releasing the fault lets the actual background sweep remove the fragment; its ledger, not GET classification, proves confirmation. Real pending DELETE separately locks editing until confirmed. A genuine backend care+reflection pass with a loopback own-key provider records paid_by own_key and identities while preserving care, then reload clears live payer and preserves stored note identity (#3270). It proves hermetic routing and receipt handling, not a real vendor bill. Controlled previous/disconnected/unrecorded destination responses and photograph403 refusal cases prove only client disclosure/retry behavior; they do not certify real remote failure states or entitlement revocation. Settings discloses exact owner-approved direct page-reading versus relay destinations before key save, with desktop/phone and enlarged text inspection. Existing receipt matrix rejects unversioned model identities while retaining prose and independent essay source (#3271). No custody/local-model/attestation/production guarantee is claimed. #3305 additionally arranges only the missing vault_destination of an actually ingested synthetic page, reproducing a pre-binding copy. Real DELETE records an unrecorded pending obligation; real save and Finish return the same destination-free409 and show neutral hints at phone/desktop enlarged text. A deep-shelf retry exposes the real refusal; pointer/keyboard local-only erase leaves an unconfirmed obligation and a fragment still present in the recording vault. Glyph bounds and recovery targets are observed independently of those state receipts.

A real outgoing-account habit POST is held while the user logs out and signs into another account in the same running app. Delivering its success or a controlled lost reply must not replace the incoming account habits or send old sibling updates. A real incoming-account create remains usable, and both incoming rows survive reload. Phone and desktop browser witnesses cover success and failure; real manager/store/scoped disk tests cover both create entrypoints, ABA, queued logs, missing credentials and compensation. The same phone and desktop account-switch journey also holds a real paginated GET after proving its answer contains the outgoing account row. That answer is delivered only after the incoming list is visible; the incoming row remains and the outgoing row stays absent before any incoming mutation can conceal stale hydration. Actual manager/storage integration additionally covers delayed cache reads, recovery and replay credentials, and both old replies and new work during adoption, logout and re-authentication wipes. A captured current-session check-in receiving a controlled 401 renews through the real auth endpoint, retries the same payload with its renewed credential, and persists through reload. Phone and desktop browser witnesses cover renewal; manager and scoped storage controls cover pinned mutator retries and durable create confirmation.

A user sets a daily reminder on a habit (PUT /habits/{habit_id} carries the cadence; the reminder itself is scheduled on the device through expo-notifications), then signs out or another account signs in on the same phone (#3334). Logout and account-switch cleanup cancel the reminders on the device as well as their on-device records; a reschedule that was still in flight when the account moved withdraws whatever it scheduled instead of recording it under the incoming account, including after A to B to A; and the next account's start-up reconcile cancels any reminder a failed logout cancel left behind. Uncovered because local notification scheduling is native-only: the web build has no scheduler, so no browser spec can observe a reminder being scheduled or cancelled, and no supported native runtime is in the e2e lane. Pinned meanwhile by src/features/Habits/__tests__/habitReminderOwnership.test.ts, which holds the native schedule, cancel and bookkeeping calls open over the real notification storage and account scope (A to B, A to B to A, mid-cleanup settle, cancellation failure, late scheduling success, bookkeeping failure, notification-off, logout and restart reconcile, plus same-account success and failure controls), and by src/features/Habits/__tests__/useHabitNotifications.test.ts. That is evidence about what the app asks the native module to do against a Jest mock, not certification of any OS scheduler's inventory.

A real habit POST is held while the account's token is revoked on the real server; the running app's next read is refused, its refresh is refused, and the same account signs back in through the re-auth sheet without its id changing. The new session hydrates the account's real rows, then the held create's lost reply (phone) or success (desktop) is delivered: the row the new session shows never vanishes, and the ended session sends nothing further under its revoked credential. A reload shows the same single row. AuthProvider integration covers append, insert and logging across a real onUnauthorized and same-owner sign-in, the pending re-auth window, and controls for an uninterrupted session and a legitimate token refresh.

Due-review reflection dismissals are account-owned on this device (#3289), proved in a real browser (#3321). Two accounts are rewound in the lane database so GET /reflections/due names the same scope, c1:w1, for both: the collision an unscoped flag would turn into one account's decline hiding the other's card. Account A sets its mounted Weekly Review card aside with the real Not now control (keyboard on phone, pointer on desktop); the only record written is A's @adepthood/reflection_dismissed:c1:w1#u<A> in on-device storage, no reflection write request is sent, and after reload the server still names c1:w1 while the shelf offers the daily page instead. An unscoped legacy flag for the same scope with unknown ownership is then planted, A's next real due read is answered by the server and held from the app, and B signs in through Settings in the same running SPA: B's independently due card stays offered, the late A answer is delivered without hiding or re-deciding it, and the legacy flag stays unassigned rather than migrating to B. B's undeclined card survives B's own reload, and A, B, A returns A to its retained set-aside. The decline's keyboard reach, pointer actionability and viewport containment are asserted at normal and doubled text, at 390 and 1280. The held read lands after a logout that remounts the signed-in tree, so the hook's owner/generation guards are not the only line there; their mounted-replacement cases stay in useDueReviewOwnership.test.tsx. #3073's broader criteria are not claimed here.

A reader signs up through the real client and checks the shared local date shortcuts in photograph capture and Habits onboarding. Real account/habit reads supply the application surfaces; date selection itself is a local draft, not a claimed saved program-date mutation or transcription request. Phone and desktop normal/doubled shortcut text retain complete labels, separate 44px targets, range-disabled future choices and distinct Tab/Enter/Space actions. The browser measures DOM glyph/parent/viewport bounds and inspects saved frames. Targeted text doubling does not establish physical OS zoom or native certification.

A user leaves the shared date picker open across local midnight and the quick choices answer for the day it now is, not the day the picker mounted (#3381). The covering spec signs up through the real client in America/Los_Angeles, seeds one habit, moves the page clock to 23:59 on the next Sunday and opens the Energy Scaffolding date step, then moves the wall clock past midnight with setSystemTime so no timer fires and nothing re-renders the picker. Pressing next monday commits the following week's Monday, today commits Monday, and first of next month commits the first of the month after Monday's, at 390px and 1280px. Unmounted-clock edge cases stay in Jest (src/components/__tests__/DatePicker.test.tsx): the month boundary, maxDate/minDate/disabledDate re-evaluated on the next render, a stale-rendered enabled button that now falls outside maxDate committing nothing, and first of next month anchored to local midnight so a maxDate on that day keeps it enabled. Date selection here is a local draft, not a saved program-date mutation.

A practitioner adopts Body Scan through the catalog and saves a real manual sitting before accepting the optional once-per-adoption habit invitation (#3153). The actual app uses the shared canonical habit manager and timer eligibility predicate. A new habit is created through the shared goal editor with one session per tier four times per week, explicitly revealed, then its server-confirmed ID is linked to the caller-owned adoption. The first link attempt is aborted by the harness; retry reuses the saved row, remains disabled during a held real PATCH, clears the prior failure claim while pending, and adopts only its confirmed response. Later completed timed and manual sittings add one session each; only the real timer marks via_timer. The link and additive total survive reload, clearing persists through the same adoption PATCH, and a previously answered offer does not reappear. A second real journey links an already-owned minutes habit arranged through the API; while that real PATCH is held, Cancel is disabled and dimmed and neither it nor Escape (the modal's onRequestClose) closes the picker, so a pending choice can never look cancelled and then land anyway (#3382). It then logs seven user-entered minutes without inventing timer origin and five real timer minutes additively, then aborts only the optional habit POST while the real practice POST still saves. The factual failure notice offers Try logging again, which resends the refused write under its original Idempotency-Key once the route is restored. Every sitting re-reads GET /habits/ before preparing its habit write (#3384): after another device moves the habit to sessions through PUT /habits/{habit_id}/goals/units while the screen stays mounted, a nine-minute sitting posts completed_units 1, never 9; when that read is aborted, no goal completion is posted, a factual notice says the practice is saved, and its retry posts one current session. Reload and authenticated verification-only GET /practice-sessions/ prove all six sittings persisted and the habit holds exactly the confirmed units. Phone390 and desktop1280 original frames, normal and doubled rendered text, glyph bounds and 44px control geometry validate the new invitation, picker, shared goals and factual failure notice. Mounted controls additionally cover duplicate creation taps, reuse of an already saved habit after a refused link, account ABA and missing credential masking. Browser evidence does not certify native geometry or physical-device lifecycle.

A writer on a short phone page -- 200% browser zoom on a 390px phone, 195x422 CSS px at device scale 2 -- opens a new page and meets every length the idle writing timer offers (#3403). The presets wrap to a second row there, and the floating band used to keep its resonance-sized lift and hide 30, 45 and the unit behind an inner scroll nobody could see. The band now gives up that lift when its content cannot fit above it, and keeps it everywhere it can. The real browser reads each preset's box and the unit's against the band's visible area and the viewport with the band unscrolled, hit-tests each one's centre, keeps every preset at the 44px floor, then taps 30 where it is drawn and walks 10, 20, 30, 45 by Tab, each in view as it takes focus, choosing 45 with Enter (the readout says 30:00, then 45:00). The same checks run at 1280x720, at 390x844, and at 390x844 with the timer's text doubled. Jest pins the lowering, its no-flip re-measure, and the page clearance it reserves in WritingSessionSurface.

A writer opens a draft at 390x844, at the same physical size under 200% browser zoom (195x422 CSS px at device scale 2), and at 1280x800 (#3456). Before the writer asks the timer to run, phone layouts dock its complete 10/20/30/45-minute tray below the paper instead of floating it over the body; the desktop keeps the established margin rail. The browser proves the timer and textarea have zero overlap in every painted frame from the moment the page opens, not only once layout settles: the docked tray stays unpainted and untouchable until the page has reserved its measured height (#3481). The entire phone tray remains inside the viewport, and Finish receives elementFromPoint hits across its full height after the page is scrolled to its beginning, midpoint and end. Starting the timer returns the existing running surface to its absolute floating band and hit-tests Stop, so #3132's running behavior is not traded away. At the more severe 390x300 physical split-screen under effective 200% (195x150 CSS px), the idle tray is capped inside the viewport and scrolls internally: the browser proves real overflow, hit-tests Start at the top and 45 at the bottom, and retains paired top/bottom frames showing every timer control reachable. Before/after frames are retained under e2e/artifacts/journal-idle-timer-3456 and e2e/artifacts/pr3468-review-followup for human visual review.

An authenticated writer sees the payer before an ask. The browser checks real server-confirmed armed demo readings and first letters with Demo disclosure, persistence, no wallet charge and no provider calls, plus explicitly controlled production app-provider keyless reading/letter Settings paths without a UI ask, real deployment-owner vault readings charged to the wallet with and without a key, wallet-priced vault first letters with explicit price acknowledgment and free cached reopening, missing-capability refusal without charge or app-provider fallback, and app-provider own-key reading receipts without a wallet debit. A controlled rolling-server response omitting only route metadata proves unknown payment disables asking. A separate explicitly controlled empty-wallet response changes only affordability while preserving the real owner route: optional EXPO_PUBLIC_CREDIT_PACK_URL set/unset determines the exact link and same-email note, and the press sends only one keyless POST ?free_only=true, which the funded real server refuses 409 resonance_payment_unconfirmed rather than charge, with no wallet change. The same controlled empty wallet still lets the real server adjudicate its free exits (#3389): a page made intimate from another device after the screen loaded shows the server's privacy reason, and a locally flagged page shows the reviewed care surface, each with no wallet change and no vault reflection or letter dial. Admission is bound to the disclosed payer route (#3385): a controlled usage read serves the app-provider route a key-holding writer saw before their vault connected, and the real server refuses that reading 409 resonance_payment_unconfirmed and that first letter 409 essay_price_unacknowledged, with no wallet, vault or provider side effect, while the client rereads the real route and shows the new credit price under a nothing-was-charged notice; confirming it then sends disclosed_route=vault_bound and spends exactly one credit for each. A first letter priced against that controlled empty wallet, with and without a saved key, offers no ask and no Settings arm: it names when the balance returns, that a vault-written letter uses credits even with a saved key, and, only when EXPO_PUBLIC_CREDIT_PACK_URL is set, the pack link (opened by keyboard) and same-email note (#3386); Not now, pressed by keyboard, closes it with no essay POST, no wallet change and no vault dial. On both empty-wallet surfaces the cancel arm announces what it actually declines -- closing without buying credits, or just closing -- never a key that is not on the card (#3388). Phone390 and desktop1280 computed text at200 percent are inspected with actual pointer hit testing.

A vault-bound writer with their own Anthropic or OpenAI key, whose managed vault advertises request_key_providers (Creek contract 0.18, Creek-Vault ADR-0015), asks for a reading (#3437, ADR 0009 2026-10-16 amendment). The browser spec saves the key in Settings and sees the managed-vault sentence in the key disclosure; the price line before the reading says "Your vault will write this reading with your own Anthropic key" and the receipt after it says "Paid by your own Anthropic key, through your vault"; the real server answers paid_by own_key with own_key_vendor anthropic and draws nothing from the wallet; and the lane vault's ledger shows the key arrived by digest on POST /v1/reflections and on no other call. The managed-vault offer's notice, reached through the real Settings -> vault -> create path with only activation availability controlled, says what happens to the key and the writing. The backend matrix (backend/tests/security/test_ai_boundary_network_matrix.py) pins the rest: the writer dials only their vault, the key rides only reflections, letters and the classification pass, a self-connected vault is never sent it and still takes a credit, an intimate entry dials nothing, and a canary key never reaches a response, a log record or a table.

A writer finishes a journal entry, reopens it with the pencil and chooses Edit, and can finish it again (#3447). The covering spec writes and finishes a page through the real client, presses the exit row's Edit, confirms Edit, types a line and waits for the real autosave, then finds Finish under the body with at least a 44px target, at 390x844, 1280x800 and 390px at 200% browser zoom (195x422 CSS px at device scale 2). No autosave PATCH during the edit sends status draft. Pressing Finish sends one PATCH /journal/{id} carrying the edited body and status finished, and the page returns to reading with the pencil back in the exit row and no body field. On that finished read view, the same three frames sweep the API-key, Edit, Close, Promote a quote and Get resonance siblings; the browser measures the Promote button and every label glyph inside the paper, rejects sideways page overflow, and uses a Range for each word so wrapping at spaces passes while a mid-word split fails (#3457). Jest pins that Finish stays withheld while the edited page is empty and that the read action's row, button and label can all yield inside the 195 CSS-pixel column.

A newly signed-in writer opens Settings and sees the honest gain beneath each optional depth before its switch (#3106): one habit begins at one minute across three weeks, a practice grows from one minute to 45 minutes across its arc, the Course offers ten capacities at calendar pace, and Sangha offers company whose point is the room the writer is actually in. The configured Sangha door leads with that company before saying the app works without it once, while preserving the one-tap decline hint. The vault row and screen lead with the bounded sorting gain before optional-vault mechanics; the browser crosses the real depth-preference, vault-connection and managed-activation reads, preserves the custody and Intimate disclosures, and proves the gain-to-floor reading order. At 390x844, the same physical size under effective 200% (195x422 CSS pixels at device scale 2), and 1280x800, it rejects horizontal text clipping and sideways document overflow, keeps one reachable switch in every depth row, and retains before/after frames for human inspection.

A writer finishes an entry containing open and nested checked tasks, then ticks the open task directly in read mode without reopening Edit (#3448). The checkbox keeps the existing glyph and dimmed checked-line treatment, exposes its item text and checked state to assistive technology, and has an expanded press target. Its optimistic one-character state swap sends a message-only PATCH through the serialized journal write lane; a cold reload shows both tasks checked while the entry remains finished. The real-client browser journey also delays that PATCH while the writer enters Edit and proves newer typed text survives the response and autosaves, delays an editor PATCH while the writer presses Close and proves text typed after X is durable before navigation, then refuses a task PATCH and its Close-time retry to prove the entry stays open with Retry reachable until persistence succeeds. It saves evidence at 390x844, effective 200% phone zoom and 1280x800 desktop.

A writer opens the Journal home on a 390px phone at 200% browser zoom (195x422 CSS px at device scale 2) and reads the Today's habits and Practices stat tiles without a word split across lines (#3440). The covering spec signs up through the real client, waits for both tiles to show their real counts from GET /habits/ and GET /practice-sessions/insights, and measures every word of each tile's title, stat and cue with a Range: all of a word's client rects share one line top.
